root.name: Benko Gambit: Nd2 Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 b5 4. cxb5 a6 5. bxa6 Bxa6 6. Nc3 d6 7. Nf3 g6 8. Nd2

overview: Black has sacrificed the b-pawn for pressure on the a- and b-files, and White's 8.Nd2 aims for Nc4 and a quick g3 or e4 set-up while guarding against ...Bxf1. Black develops with ...Bg7, ...Qa5 or ...Nbd7 and keeps the queenside pressure.

white_ideas.idea: Hold the extra pawn by consolidating with Nd2-c4 and g3/Bg2
Trade off Black's active pieces and neutralise the open files

black_ideas.idea: Pressure the a- and b-files with rooks and queen
Fianchetto the dark-squared bishop and aim at White's queenside

typical_structures.structure: Benko pawn structure with White d5 pawn and Black c5/d6
Open a- and b-files for Black rooks

character.notes: Positional, long-term compensation rather than forcing tactics.

gambit.notes: Black has given the b-pawn and White can keep it, as in the Benko generally.

soundness.notes: The Benko is sound; Nd2 is a quiet attempt to keep the pawn.

structure.notes: Half-open a- and b-files and a locked d5/c5 centre.

level.notes: Compensation is positional and takes judgement more than theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Qa5 line
sublines_that_differ.how: Black aims at c3 and Nd2, a more active version than ...Bg7.

character.reason: Black's compensation is positional pressure, not an immediate attack, and White has a calm plan.

gambit.reason: Black gives the b-pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.reason: The Benko is a sound gambit and this line is a quiet way to meet it.

structure.reason: Half-open queenside files and a fixed centre give a semi-open character.

approach.reason: A respected gambit defence at all levels.

level.reason: Compensation is judged positionally rather than learned as a forcing line.

plans.reason: Black's g7 bishop aims along the long diagonal at White's queenside.
